evidence: The paper uses random forests only as a classifier to achieve predictions, not to extract importance measures. Results report perspective importance via classification accuracy: "inflorescence (87.3%), ligule front (75.1%), ligule side (70.3%), node (64.9%), leaf back (63.9%) and leaf top (62.6%)" derived from training separate models on each perspective. Conclusions rest on accuracy differences and cross-classifier consistency: "the strip-like patterns...indicate that the feature descriptors and the classifiers largely agree on which species are easy to classify" (Figure 6).
